obligation: PHMSA immediate telephone notice of a gathering line accident
trigger: A release from the 14-mile regulated rural gathering line resulting in an event described in 195.50 that caused a death or injury requiring hospitalization, an unintended fire or explosion, estimated property damage (including cleanup and lost product) over $50,000, pollution of a water body as described in 195.52(a)(4), or that the operator judges significant; for example, a release after manipulated pump station setpoints
deadline: At the earliest practicable moment following discovery, and no later than 1 hour after confirmed discovery
notify: National Response Center by telephone (800-424-8802), with the information listed in 195.52(b), including an initial estimate of product released under the written procedure in 195.52(c)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - regulated trunk line (14 miles). Not required for the 78 miles of reporting-regulated-only lines (195.15(c)(2)). Pipeline Compliance Manager decides; the cyber investigation never delays it (POL-03 4.6)

obligation: PHMSA revised or confirmed telephone notice
trigger: After a telephone notice under 195.52(a)
deadline: Within 48 hours after confirmed discovery, to the extent practicable: revise or confirm the release estimate, location, time, fatalities and injuries, and other significant facts
notify: National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - regulated trunk line. Use the manual fallback (LACT tickets, tank gauges, line pack tables) if SCADA data is unavailable or untrusted (POAM-020)

trigger: A failure with a release resulting in any of the events in 195.50: an unintended explosion or fire; a release of 5 gallons or more (with a maintenance exception under 5 barrels); a death; an injury requiring hospitalization; or estimated property damage over $50,000
deadline: As soon as practicable, but not later than 30 days after discovery of the accident; supplemental report within 30 days of new or changed information
notify: PHMSA (DOT Form 7000-1)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 92 miles: the regulated trunk line and the reporting-regulated-only lines (195.15)

trigger: A safety-related condition listed in 195.55(a), including any malfunction or operating error that causes pipeline pressure to rise above 110 percent of MOP (195.55(a)(4)), for example after an unauthorized setpoint change; exceptions in 195.55(b) (including conditions that become a reportable accident or are repaired before the deadline)
deadline: Received by PHMSA within 5 working days after an operator representative first determines the condition exists, and not later than 10 working days after discovery
notify: PHMSA by email as directed in 195.56(a)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 92 miles, unless a 195.55(b) exception applies. Pipeline Compliance Manager decides

obligation: Oil discharge notice to the National Response Center
trigger: A discharge of oil that may be harmful under 40 CFR 110.3 (violates water quality standards, or causes a film, sheen, or discoloration on the water or adjoining shorelines, or a sludge or emulsion); for example a tank overflow or flow line release after loss of SCADA control
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge has knowledge of the discharge
notify: National Response Center (800-424-8802); if not practicable, the Coast Guard or EPA on-scene coordinator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - any company facility (tank batteries, flow lines, gathering system). HSE Director makes the call; a gathering line release may need both this and the 195.52 notice

citation: State oil and gas program rules and permit conditions (Florida and Alabama); emergency response plan
trigger: A release of oil or produced water, or injection pressure above a permit limit, caused by a cyber event
deadline: Per the permit conditions and the state program rules listed in the emergency response plan
notify: State oil and gas and environmental agencies as listed in the emergency response plan
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational duty. HSE Director confirms the current requirement at the time of the event; not restated here

trigger: Unauthorized access to electronic personal information of Florida residents: royalty owners (names with Social Security or taxpayer numbers) or employees (Social Security, driver license, or health plan numbers)
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. A 15-day extension is available for this individual notice only if good cause is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days; delay only on a law enforcement request. No notice is required if, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm; that determination must be in writing, kept 5 years, and sent to the department within 30 days
notify: Each affected Florida resident (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if personal information was accessed. General Counsel decides with outside counsel (decision log, runbook section 6)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension applies to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if 500 or more Florida residents. About 14,000 royalty owners and 850 employees are on file, so a large breach would exceed this

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if more than 1,000 individuals are notified at once

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (production accounting, HR and payroll, telematics, outside tax vendor) has a breach
deadline: The vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after determining the breach; the company then gives the (3) to (5) notices. Production accounting and HR vendors have 5-business-day contract terms
notify: The company (General Counsel)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts; telematics and tax vendor terms being added (POAM-023)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Royalty owners or employees who reside outside Florida are affected (owners live in more than 40 states; employees in Florida and Alabama)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents, and state attorneys general or regulators where each state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - General Counsel applies the law of each state where affected individuals reside, using the owner list by state; a summary for the 10 states with the most owners is due 2027-03-31

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: No legal requirement for this company (see the TSA and CIRCIA rows); CISA and FBI reporting channels
trigger: Ransomware, any intrusion into SCADA, or an unauthorized command to field equipment
deadline: As soon as practicable; the runbooks target day 0 to 1
notify: CISA (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended; supports the OFAC mitigating factor and warns the sector. Security Manager reports through counsel

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: use the carrier's breach hotline before engaging any vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($15 million limit; $500,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal. CFO calls

trigger: An incident that affects shipper volumes, statements, the shipper portal, or shipper confidential data, or that shuts down the gathering system
deadline: Agreements have no incident notice term today (gap 8). Company practice until amended: Measurement Supervisor notifies affected shippers within 24 hours of confirming impact; force majeure notices per each agreement
notify: Each shipper's designated contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; amendment adding data handling and incident notice terms due 2027-06-30 (POAM-021)

citation: Connection agreement with the transmission pipeline; crude purchase contracts; gas purchase contracts (contracts)
trigger: An incident that stops or changes deliveries at the LACT units or the lease sales points, or affects LACT data sent to the transmission pipeline
deadline: Immediately for a receipt-point shutdown (operational call from the OCC); otherwise per each contract's notice and force majeure terms
notify: Transmission pipeline control center; crude purchasers; gas gathering companies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational. Control Room Manager (operational call) and VP Operations (contract notice)

citation: Reserve-based credit agreement; joint operating agreements; sponsor reporting terms (contracts)
trigger: An incident with material operational or financial effect, or that affects partner billing data
deadline: Per each agreement (lender notice of material adverse events; partner notices under the joint operating agreements)
notify: Bank group agent; the private equity sponsor's operating partner; 22 non-operating working interest owners
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. CFO checks each agreement with General Counsel; CEO informs the sponsor and the audit committee chair the same day for severity 1

citation: TSA SD Pipeline-2021-01G, Section II.C (N21-R02 family)
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-notified pipeline owner or operator
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company operates a gathering system but has received no TSA notification (P03 section 1). Becomes Yes on a TSA notice; the quarterly regulatory watch checks for one (POL-01 4.13)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, the company is below the SBA size standard (850 of 1,250 employees) and meets no sector criterion (P03 G-124). Recheck when final

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities / OCS facilities / vessels
trigger: Cyber incident involving or endangering a vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); 'without delay' to the National Response Center for entities not reporting under 6.16-1
notify: FBI, CISA (for any cyber incident), and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - onshore only; no vessel, waterfront facility, or OCS facility (N21-R01 not applicable, P03)

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a registrant
deadline: Form 8-K within 4 business days after determining the incident is material
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held and files no SEC reports

citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or a Kaspersky covered article identified in contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
